Rashi on Pesachim 41a:10:1.english: He is liable - [to receive] lashes for eating it.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:12:1.hebrew: ר' יוסי היא - דאמר בישול לאחר אפיה בישול הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:12:1.english: It is Rabbi Yosei - Who says [that] cooking after baking is [considered] cooking.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:12:2.hebrew: יוצאין - ידי חובת מצה ברקיק השרוי בתבשיל לאחר אפייתו, ואף על פי שמתמסמס, לחם הוא כל זמן שהוא קיים שלא נימוח לגמרי. וכן במבושל:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:12:2.english: One fulfills - [his] obligation of matza with a wafer that was soaked in a cooked dish after its baking. And even though it softens, it is [still] bread as long as it remains intact, [meaning] that it has not completely dissolved. And similarly with a boiled [wafer].

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:12:3.hebrew: אבל לא במבושל - דלאו לחם קרינא ביה, ואע"פ שכבר נאפה בתנור, הואיל וחזר ובישלו, ביטלו מתורת לחם:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:12:3.english: But not with a boiled [wafer] - For we do not call it "bread," and even though it was already baked in the oven, since he subsequently boiled it, he nullified it from the status of bread.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:13:1.hebrew: שאני הכא דרבייה קרא - ובשל מבושל, דהוי ליה למכתב "ומבושל", וגזירת הכתוב הוא בפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:13:1.english: Here it is different, as the verse included it - [By stating] “boiled, boiled” (uvashel mevushal), for it should have written [simply] “and boiled” (umevushal), and it is a scriptural decree regarding the Paschal lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:14:1.hebrew: יכול צלאו כל צרכו - ואח"כ בשלו יהא חייב, והאי תנא הוא דאמר לעיל צלאו ואח"כ בישלו חייב. לישנא אחרינא: יכול צלאו כל צרכו — דשויא חרוכא, כדמפרש — יהא חייב, דלאו צלי אש הוא אלא קלי אש ושרוף. וזה עיקר, וראשון אינו כלום; דההוא תנא, כיון דרבי קרא צלאו ואחר כך בישלו, מה לי שויה חרוכא, מה לי לא שויה:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:14:1.english: I might have thought [that if] he roasted it fully - [and] afterward boiled it, he should be liable; and this is the Tanna who said above [that if] he roasted it and afterward boiled it, he is liable. Another version: "[I might have thought that if] he roasted it fully" — meaning he charred it, as [the Gemara] explains [below] — "he should be liable," for it is not "roasted with fire," but rather parched with fire and burned. And this [second explanation] is the primary one, while the first is nothing [i.e., untenable]; for [according to] that Tanna, since the verse included [the case where] he roasted it and afterward boiled it, what difference is there whether he charred it [or] whether he did not char it?

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:16:1.english: Raw - Completely [raw], that it was not roasted at all.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:16:2.english: Partially roasted [na] - Roasted and not [fully] roasted.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:17:1.hebrew: יכול יהא מותר - לאכול ממנו חי לכתחלה, דאפילו איסורא נמי ליכא. תלמוד לומר: ״אל תאכלו ממנו נא כי אם צלי אש״ — ולא זה שאינו צלי. והויא לאו שבכללות, והאי תנא סבר: אין לוקין על לאו שבכללות:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:17:1.english: I might [have thought] that it is permitted - to eat from it raw at the outset, such that there is not even a prohibition; [therefore,] the verse states: "Do not eat of it raw... but roasted with fire" — and not this, which is not roasted. And it is a generalized prohibition, and this tanna holds [that] one does not receive lashes for a generalized prohibition.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:17:2.hebrew: כדאמרי פרסאי אברנים - אותה צליה שבלשון פרסי קרויה אברנים, בלשון הקודש קרי נא:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:17:2.english: As the Persians say: Avarnim - That roasting which in the Persian language is called avarnim is called na in the Holy Tongue.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:18:1.english: The hot springs of Tiberias - Boiling springs.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:18:2.hebrew: פסח שבישל בחמי טבריא חייב - על אכילתו, וקא סלקא דעתך משום דלא תאכל מבושל:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:18:2.english: A Paschal [lamb] that one cooked in the hot springs of Tiberias [is] liable - For eating it, and you might initially assume [that it is] because of [the prohibition], "Do not eat [it] boiled."

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:19:1.hebrew: דלאו תולדות אש היא - הלכך, לאו בישול הוא דליהוי חייב משום אב מלאכה:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:19:1.english: For it is not a fire derivative - Therefore, it is not [considered] cooking such that one would be liable on account of a primary category of [prohibited] labor.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:1:1.english: Did [the Master] say [it] regarding charoset - Do you hold that the Rabbis also disagree regarding charoset?

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:20:1.hebrew: משום צלי אש - לאו דלא תאכל כי אם צלי אש איכא, ולא לאו דבישול, וסבר לוקין על לאו שבכללות:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:20:1.english: Due to “roasted with fire” - There is the prohibition of “you shall not eat [it] except roasted with fire,” and not the prohibition of boiling; and he holds [that] one receives lashes for a general prohibition.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:21:1.english: Explicitly - That Rav Chisda held [him] liable on account of "roasted with fire" and not on account of cooking.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:3:1.hebrew: לא סבירא לי - אלא בחרוסת נמי שרו, והלכה כמותן:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:3:1.english: I do not hold [so] - Rather, they permit [it] even with charoset, and the halachah is in accordance with them.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:4:1.hebrew: כוותיה דרב כהנא מסתברא - דאמר רבנן אחרוסת לא פליגי, וכי אמר שמואל הלכה כחכמים, אחרדל קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:4:1.english: It is reasonable [to rule] in accordance with Rav Kahana - Who said [that] the Rabbis do not disagree regarding charoset, and when Shmuel said [that] the halakha is in accordance with the Sages, he said [it] regarding mustard.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:4:2.english: The halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - Who said earlier [that] vinegar shrinks them.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:4:3.hebrew: מאי לאו - מדלא צמית חטין שהתחילו לינפח כבר, אלמא כשאר משקין הוא, אחמועי נמי מחמע את הניתן מתחילה לתוכו כדרב כהנא. אלמא שמואל כרב כהנא סבירא ליה, וכי קאמר שמואל הלכה כחכמים, אחרדל קאמר ולא אחרוסת:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:4:3.english: What, isn't it - Since it does not shrink wheat that has already begun to swell, evidently it is like other liquids, [and] it also leavens [flour] that is put into it initially, in accordance with [the view of] Rav Kahana. Evidently Shmuel holds in accordance with Rav Kahana, and when Shmuel said "the halakha is in accordance with the Sages," he said it regarding mustard and not regarding charoset.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:5:1.hebrew: לא מיצמת צמית - את שהתחיל להחמיץ, ולא מחמע נמי את הניתן לתוכו, דלא הוי כמים:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:5:1.english: [It] does not cause to shrink - that which has begun to leaven, and it also does not leaven that which is placed into it, for it is not like water.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:6:1.english: In water - [This refers to the verse:] “nor boiled in any way in water.”

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:7:1.english: Which temper their taste - That they impart their taste into it.

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:8:1.hebrew: ובשל מבושל - רבויא הוא, דהוה ליה למיכתב נא ומבושל:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:8:1.english: Nor boiled in any way [lit. boiled, boiled] - It is an amplification, for [the verse] should have written “raw or boiled.”

Rashi on Pesachim 41a:9:1.hebrew: צלי קדר - שמבשלין אותו בקדירה בלא מים ובלא שום משקה, אלא מים הנפלטין משמנו. למאן דיליף לה מק"ו, הכא שרי; לרבי דיליף מרבויא, האי נמי "בשל מבושל" הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 41a:9:1.english: Roasted in a pot - That they cook it in a pot without water and without any liquid, except [for] the liquid that exudes from its fat. According to the one who derives it from a kal vachomer [a fortiori inference], here it is permitted; according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who derives [it] from an amplification [in the verse], this too is [considered] "boiled, boiled."

Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:12:1.hebrew: אמר רב כהנא הא מני ר' יוסי היא - תימה: דרב כהנא דמוקי לה כרבי יוסי, לרבנן האי "בשל מבושל" מאי עבדי להו? דצלאו ואחר כך בישלו לא צריך קרא, דמסברא ידעינן דבישול מבטל הצליה, כדאמר רבי יוסי גבי מצה. ויש לומר, דרב כהנא סבר דרבי יוסי יליף מבשל מבושל דבישול מבטל אפייה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:12:1.english: Rav Kahana said: Whose [opinion] is this? It is [that of] Rabbi Yosei - This is astonishing: since Rav Kahana establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, according to the Rabbis, what do they do with this [phrase] "boiled in any way" [bashel mevushal]? For [the case where] one roasted it and afterward boiled it does not require a verse, since from logical reasoning we know that boiling nullifies roasting, as Rabbi Yosei says regarding matzah! And one can say that Rav Kahana holds that Rabbi Yosei derives from "boiled in any way" that boiling nullifies baking.

Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:12:2.hebrew: אבל לא במבושל - פ"ה דבישול מבטל ליה מתורת לחם, ולפי' מיירי בבלילתו רכה, דבלילתו עבה לא נפיק מתורת לחם כדפירש לעיל. ור"י מפרש דמיירי בבלילתו עבה, ופסולה משום מצה עשירה; ומייתי דכי היכי דסבר רבי יוסי דבישול מפיק ליה מתורת אפייה לשוויה מצה עשירה כאילו לא נאפה, ה"נ גבי פסח עקר מיניה בישול שם צליה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:12:2.english: "But not with a boiled [wafer]" - Rashi explained that cooking nullifies it from the status of bread, and therefore [the baraita] is dealing with [a wafer] whose batter is thin, for [one] whose batter is thick does not leave the status of bread, as he explained earlier. And the Ri explains that it is dealing with [a wafer] whose batter is thick, and it is disqualified on account of [being] matza ashirah [enriched matza]; and [Rav Kahana] brings [this as proof] that just as Rabbi Yosei holds that cooking removes it from the status of baking to render it matza ashirah, as if it had not been baked, so too regarding the Paschal offering, cooking uproots from it the designation of roasting.

Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:13:1.hebrew: עולא אמר אפי' תימא ר' מאיר וכו' - הכא מדמי פסח לבישול מצה, והיינו דלא כמסקנא דכיצד מברכין (ברכות דף לח:), דקאמר התם עולא משמיה דר' יוחנן: שלקות מברכין עליהם שהכל לרבי יוסי, דאית ליה הכא גבי מצה דבישול מבטל האפיה, ה"נ בישול מבטל מהם שם ירק; ודחי: ע"כ לא קאמר רבי יוסי אלא דבעינן טעם מצה. ועולא לטעמיה, דלא בעי לדחויא הכא טעמא דרבי יוסי דבעינן טעם מצה, והתם נמי קאמר דלרבי יוסי מברך שהכל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:13:1.english: Ulla said: Even if you say Rabbi Meir, etc. - Here [the Gemara] compares the Paschal lamb to the boiling of matzah, and this is not in accordance with the conclusion of [the chapter] Keitzad Mevarkhin (Berakhot 38b), where Ulla says in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: On boiled vegetables one recites Shehakol according to Rabbi Yosei; [for just] as he holds here regarding matzah that boiling nullifies the baking, so too boiling nullifies from them the status of vegetable. And [the Gemara there] rejects [this]: Rabbi Yosei only said [that regarding matzah] because we require the taste of matzah. And Ulla is consistent with his own view, for he did not wish to reject here Rabbi Yosei's reason [by saying] that we require the taste of matzah, and there too he said that according to Rabbi Yosei one recites Shehakol.

Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:3:1.hebrew: לא שמיע לי כלומר לא סבירא לי - אף על גב דתניא כוותיה, קסבר מתניתין פליגא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:3:1.english: I did not hear [it], that is to say, I do not hold [in accordance with it] - Even though a baraita is taught in accordance with him [Rav Kahana], he holds that our Mishnah disagrees.

Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:4:1.hebrew: מדאמר שמואל אין הלכה כרבי יוסי - השתא מדמי חומץ לחרוסת, וע"כ נראה לר"י דעולא, דאמר לעיל: "בין כך ובין כך אסור משום 'לך לך אמרינן נזירא, סחור סחור לכרמא לא תקרב'", פליג אדרב כהנא; דהא רב כהנא דאמר "אבל לתוך חרוסת — לדברי הכל ישרף", ולעולא לא אסר אלא משום "לך לך אמרינן":
Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:4:1.english: From [the fact] that Shmuel said, "The halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei" - Now [the Gemara] compares vinegar to charoset, and therefore it appears to the Ri that Ulla, who said above: "Either way it is prohibited because of 'Go, go, we say to the nazirite; go around, go around, do not approach the vineyard,'" disagrees with Rav Kahana; for Rav Kahana said, "But [if put] into charoset, according to all opinions it must be burned," whereas according to Ulla, he only prohibited [it] because of "Go, go, we say [to the nazirite]."

Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:4:2.hebrew: מאי לאו מדלא מצמת מחמע - קשה לר"י, דלעיל קאמר י"א: "אף נותן את החומץ ואח"כ וכו'", ופריך: ולוקמא כר' יוסי דאמר "שורן בחומץ וחומץ צומתן". משמע דתנא קמא דיש אומרים היינו ת"ק דר' יוסי, דלית ליה דחומץ צמית; ואפילו הכי קאמר: "נותן הקמח ואח"כ נותן את החומץ". אלמא קסבר אע"ג דלא צמית, חמועי נמי לא מחמע. ואור"י, דלעיל איירי לפי המסקנא דהכא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:4:2.english: What, is it not [the case that] since it does not shrink [the grain], it leavens [it]? - This is difficult for Rabbi Yitzchak: for above, [the baraita] states, "Some say: One may even put in the vinegar and afterwards [the flour]," etc., and [the Gemara] asks: Let us establish it in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who says, "One soaks them in vinegar, and vinegar shrinks them." This implies that the Tanna Kamma of "Some say" is [identical to] the Tanna Kamma of Rabbi Yosei, who does not hold that vinegar shrinks [grain]; and even so, he says, "One puts in the flour and afterwards puts in the vinegar." Thus, he holds [that] even though it does not shrink [the grain], it does not leaven [it] either. And Rabbi Yitzchak says that [the Gemara] above is speaking according to the conclusion here [that vinegar neither shrinks nor leavens].

Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:6:1.hebrew: אין מבשלים את הפסח לא במשקין וכו' - תימה למה שנאו כאן? אי משום דתנא ירקות שלוקות ומבושלות, א"כ מיד היה לו לשנות בסמוך אחריה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:6:1.english: "One may not boil the Paschal lamb in liquids, etc." - [It is] astonishing: why did [the Tanna] teach it here? If [it is] because he taught [earlier about] stewed and boiled vegetables, if so, he should have taught [it] immediately adjacent after it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:9:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו צלי קדר - פי': אי לוקה עליו אי לא, אבל לכולי עלמא פסול הוי, ועשה נמי אית ביה, דצלי מחמת ד"א הוא, כדאמרינן בריש כיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים עה:): "נטף מרוטבו על החרס וחזר עליו — יטול את מקומו; נגע בחרסו של תנור — יקלוף את מקומו". וכן שאר משקין — לא איצטריך למילף אלא לענין מלקות, אבל פשיטא דלכל הפחות איכא עשה ד"כי אם צלי אש". וא"ת: והיכי יליף שאר משקין מק"ו, והא אין מזהירין מן הדין? ויש לומר דהאי קל וחומר אינו אלא מגלה דבישול דקרא איירי אף בשאר משקין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41a:9:1.english: The practical difference between them is [with regard to] meat roasted in a pot - Explanation: [The difference is] whether one receives lashes for it or not, but according to everyone it is disqualified, and there is also [a violation of] a positive commandment in it, because it is roasted by means of something else [rather than directly by fire], as we say at the beginning of [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (below, Pesachim 75b): "[If] some of its gravy dripped onto the earthenware and returned onto it — he must remove its place; [if] it touched the earthenware of the oven — he must peel away its place." And similarly, [regarding] other liquids, it was only necessary to derive [them] with respect to lashes, for it is obvious that at the very least there is the positive commandment of "except roasted with fire" [Exodus 12:9]. And if you ask: How can it derive other liquids from a kal vachomer (an a fortiori argument), given that we do not derive a prohibition from a logical inference? One can say that this kal vachomer merely reveals that the "boiling" [written] in the verse refers even to other liquids.
